is: the sounds the world's data names (surfaces, rooms, things) and the picker's brief for every sound on a picking page: the catalogue (data/sound/catalogue.json) lays each entry here over its own, so a field here wins. 'pick' is the picker's alone: the category sets the loudness a take is brought to (tools/sound/loudness/), 'level' is how loud it is played in LUFS (its volume_db is set from it when a take is picked), 'where' is shown on the page, 'search' is what the sources are asked for. 'near' (metres, only where named) is how far out a placed sound plays at its full level before it falls off with distance, for a source far louder than a room's (a lift-off); any other falls off past 10 m, Godot's unit size (tools/usd/sound.py NEAR_METRES). A name with no file plays nothing until the owner picks one (tools/sound/picker/). Retired on 2026-10-21 (owner: every old library sound withdrawn, remade fresh): every pick (its file, its volume_db and the picker's `chosen`) went with the old sounds; each brief stays, so the sound row makes it fresh (one MOSS take) in the remake batch
